entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri S. K. Meena, Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Harish Singh Rathore, Government Advocate for the
 respondent/State.

Heard on I.A. No.5271/2025, which is first application under Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.) for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant - Thakur Katariya.

The appellant has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(N), 376(3) and 344 of IPC alongwith Sections 5(l)/6 and 5(j)(ii)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 07 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-,
RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- , life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-, RI for 03 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/- and life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the allegation against the appellant is of committing rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
Counsel for appellant argued that the prosecutrix was a consenting party as she herself had gone alongwith the appellant and stayed with him for about 15 days and made consensual relationship.

He argued that appellant 2 CRA-9455-2023 has been convicted in the case on the basis of age of the prosecutrix, as her age was found to be less than 15 years, which has been proved by the prosecution on the basis of scholar register though, the prosecution has not proved the source of recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register.
He further argued that age of the appellant was also 22 years at the time of incident.
Appellant has already remained in jail for more than 04 years.
Final hearing of the appeal may take time hence, it is prayed that the appellant be granted bail.
Counsel for the State opposed the application and prays for its rejection.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration all the facts in entirety,

1 statement of the prosecutrix from which it is clear that she was a consenting party, we find that the prosecution has failed to establish the source of recording of her age in the scholar register.

entities.text: Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from that, the appellant was also 22 years of age at the time of incident and he has already remained in jail for more than 04 years.
Appeal is of the year 2023 and final hearing of the same may take time.

In the case o f Tejubai Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75, it has been held that if the date of birth of the prosecutrix in the school register is recorded on the basis of a person who made entry of the date of birth, the same is not sufficient to prove the age.

entities.text: Tejubai Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the same, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.5271/2025 is allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Thakur 3 CRA-9455-2023 Katariya shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 21.07.2026 and all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
With the aforesaid, IA No.5271/2025 stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
